item.description: Canvas LMS is a learning management system from Instructure for course
item.content:encoded:
Canvas LMS is a learning management system from Instructure for course management, collaboration, and assessment in educational institutions.

Versions: 8.0.0 P1

Identities ❌ | Accounts ✔️ | Groups ✔️ | App Roles ✔️ | Entitlements ❌

Overview​

This section describes the Canvas objects that matter for access management. Later sections configure G&L to collect them.

Account-Level Roles

  • Users at the Account Level: Users are created at the account level, representing individuals within the entire Canvas LMS system.
  • Account-Level Roles: Different roles are assigned to users at the account level.
    • Administrator: Manages system settings, users, and courses at the institutional level.
    • Account Manager: Oversees account-level settings and user management.
    • Support: Assists users with technical support.

Course-Level Roles

  • Users at the Course Level: Users are enrolled in specific courses within the Canvas LMS. These users may include teachers, students, teaching assistants (TAs), and other roles.
  • Course-Level Roles: Different roles are assigned to users at the course level.
    • Teacher: Manages and instructs a specific course, with permissions for content creation, grading, and communication.
    • Student: Enrolls in and participates in courses, with access to assignments, discussions, and materials.
    • TA (Teaching Assistant): Assists teachers with course management and grading.

Relationship Between Users and Roles

  • At both the account and course levels, users are assigned roles to define their access and permissions within the system.
  • Users can have different roles at the account and course levels simultaneously. For example, an individual might be an administrator at the account level and a teacher in specific courses.

Permissions and Responsibilities Roles dictate the permissions and responsibilities of users. For instance, a Teacher at the course level can manage content, grade assignments, and interact with students within the confines of that course, while an Administrator at the account level has broader control over system-wide settings and user management.

Application​

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Application.
  3. Click on Create Application and select Other Application.
  4. Enter the details as shown below.
  5. Click Finish.

Account Collector​

This section explains the process for configuring an account collector for the Canvas application. We will use the RSA G&L Generic REST collector for this purpose.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Applications.
  3. Click on Canvas.
  4. Navigate to Collectors tab and click on Create Account Collector. Enter the details as shown below.

  5. Click Next and enter the connection details. This article will use Token based authentication to invoke REST APIs.

    💡Tip

    Canvas APIs do not support data filtering and hence collections may sometimes return a 504 Gateway Time-out error. A suitable time out settings in the collector might be needed.

  6. Click Next. Select the data types that the collector will be collecting from Canvas.

  7. Click Next. On the Account Data page, enter the following configurations.




    Request
    MethodGET
    URL/api/v1/accounts/self/users
    Request Headers
    Acceptapplication/json
    AuthorizationBearer ${AuthenticationToken}
    Response Mappings
    AccountId$.*.login_id
    Id$.*.id
    SISId$.*.sis_user_id
  8. Click Next. On the Group Data page, enter the following configurations.




    note

    /api/v1/users/self/groups returns the groups that the token's user belongs to, not every group in the account.

    Request
    MethodGET
    URL/api/v1/users/self/groups
    Request Headers
    Acceptapplication/json
    AuthorizationBearer ${AuthenticationToken}
    Response Mappings
    GroupId$.*.name
    Id$.*.id
    Description$.*.description
  9. Click Next. On the Account Group Membership page, enter the following configurations.




    Request
    MethodGET
    URL/api/v1/groups/${Id}/users
    Request Headers
    Acceptapplication/json
    AuthorizationBearer ${AuthenticationToken}
    Response Mappings
    Account Identifier$.*.id
  10. Click Next. In the Map Collector Attributes to Account Attributes, map the collected account attributes.

  11. Click Next. In the Map Collector Attributes to Account Mapping Attributes, map the user reference attribute.

  12. Click Next. In the Map Collector Attributes to Group Attributes, map the collected group attributes.

  13. Click Next. In the User Resolution Rules, map the user to account.

  14. Click Next. In the Member Account Resolution Rules, map the account attribute.

    info

    This value MUST always be mapped to the Account Name for any generic REST collector.

  15. Click Finish. Use the Test function to make sure the configurations are accurate.

Entitlement Collector​

This section explains the process for configuring an entitlement collector to collect roles from Canvas. We will use the RSA G&L Generic REST collector for this purpose.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as AveksaAdmin.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Applications.
  3. Click on Canvas.
  4. Navigate to Collectors tab and click on Create Entitlement Collector. Enter the details as shown below.

  5. Click Next and enter the connection details as shown in Step 5 of Account Collector.
  6. Click Next. Select the data types that the collector will be collecting from Canvas.

  7. Click Next. On the App Role Data page, enter the following configurations.




    Request
    MethodGET
    URL/api/v1/accounts/self/roles
    Request Headers
    Acceptapplication/json
    AuthorizationBearer ${AuthenticationToken}
    Response Mappings
    ApplicationRoleId$.*.role
    Id$.*.id
  8. Click Next. On the App-Role Account Membership collection page, enter the following configurations.




    Request
    MethodGET
    URL/api/v1/accounts/self/admins
    Request Headers
    Acceptapplication/json
    AuthorizationBearer ${AuthenticationToken}
    Response Mappings
    App-Role Identifier$.*.role_id
    Account Identifier$.*.user.id
  9. Click Next. In the Map Collector Attributes to App Role Attributes, map the collected account attributes.

  10. Click Next. In the Account Evaluation, map the account collector to account value.

  11. Click Next and then click Finish. Use the Test function to make sure the configurations are accurate.

Application Setup​

This section explains the process for setting up application for API access with G&L.

Steps

  1. Login to Canvas console with administrative access.
  2. Navigate to Settings https://instance.instructure.com/profile/settings.
  3. Under Approved Integrations, click on New Access Token.
  4. Specify the Purpose and leave the Expires blank. Click Generate Token.

  5. Copy the token for use with G&L.

References​

  • Canvas LMS REST API: all resources
  • Users
  • Groups
  • Admins
  • Accounts

item.content:encoded:
Aha! is product roadmap software for setting product strategy, prioritizing features, and managing development work.

Identities ❌ | Accounts ✔️ | Groups ✔️ | App Roles ❌ | Entitlements ❌

Users in Aha! represent individuals who are part of your organization and interact with the platform. Each user has their own role and permissions, which determine their level of access and the actions they can perform within Aha!. Users can be product managers, designers, developers, stakeholders, and more.

Products in Aha! represent the offerings that your company is developing and managing. A product can be a software application, a physical product, a service, or any other offering. Products are the core entities around which you plan, track features, set strategies, and manage roadmaps.

Teams in Aha! refer to groups of users who collaborate on specific products or projects. Teams are designed to facilitate efficient cross-functional work and alignment. A team might consist of product managers, developers, designers, marketers, and other roles relevant to the product's development and success.

The relationship between these elements can be summarized as follows:

Users are individuals who have access to the Sentry platform. Each user has a unique account and can be assigned specific roles and permissions that determine their level of access and actions they can perform within the organization. Users can be developers, administrators, or other team members involved in monitoring and resolving issues.

Teams are groups of users who collaborate on specific projects and share responsibilities. A team typically represents a functional unit within the organization, such as a development team, operations team, or customer support team. Teams help manage access control, streamline communication, and group users with similar responsibilities together.

Projects are individual software applications, services, or components that you want to monitor and track for errors and issues. Each project represents a unique codebase or software entity. Errors and events related to a project are collected, analyzed, and presented within the context of that project. Projects can belong to one or more teams, depending on the organizational structure.

Relationships between these components:

  • Users and Teams: Users belong to one or more teams. This association helps define which projects a user can access and what actions they can perform within those projects. Teams provide a way to manage user access and collaboration efficiently.

  • Teams and Projects: Teams can be assigned to one or more projects. This allows multiple teams to work on different aspects of a project or collaborate on multiple projects simultaneously. Teams define who has access to specific projects and contribute to error tracking and resolution efforts.

  • Users and Projects: Users who belong to teams associated with a project can access and work on that project. They can view error reports, manage issues, and collaborate with other team members to address software problems.

CyberArk is a privileged access management platform. It stores and manages privileged accounts, credentials, and secrets.

The type of data that can be collected includes accounts, safes, privileged accounts, platforms etc. 

Identities ❌ | Accounts ✔️ | Groups ✔️ | App Roles ✔️ | Entitlements ❌

Accounts - Accounts in CyberArk refer to the privileged accounts or credentials that are stored, managed, and secured within the CyberArk vault. These accounts are typically used to access and manage privileged resources such as servers, databases, applications, or network devices. Accounts can include credentials like usernames, passwords, SSH keys, API keys, or other authentication information necessary for privileged access.

Users - Users in CyberArk refer to the individuals who interact with the CyberArk solution itself. These users are typically administrators or end-users who perform various tasks related to managing and utilizing the CyberArk platform. Users have different roles and permissions within CyberArk, determining their access levels and privileges for functions such as managing accounts, configuring policies, generating reports, and conducting audits.

Groups - Groups in CyberArk are logical collections or containers used to organize users and assign permissions and access rights in a more efficient and manageable manner. Instead of individually assigning permissions to each user, administrators can create groups and assign permissions to the group. This way, any user added to the group automatically inherits the group's permissions. Groups help simplify administration and access control management in large-scale deployments by allowing administrators to manage permissions at a group level rather than on a per-user basis.

Safes - Safes in CyberArk refer to secure storage containers within the CyberArk vault where privileged accounts and sensitive information are stored. Safes act as encrypted repositories that protect and control access to the stored credentials and other sensitive data. Safes are typically organized based on the target systems, applications, or business units they relate to. By storing privileged accounts in safes, organizations can enforce strict access controls, audit all access and activity, and enable secure automatic retrieval of credentials when needed.

Users Users are individuals who have an account on the GitLab SaaS platform. Each user has a unique username and email address associated with their account. Users can belong to multiple groups and have different roles within those groups or projects.

Groups Groups in GitLab SaaS allow for organizing projects and users. A group can include multiple projects and members, enabling efficient management and collaboration across related repositories. Groups provide a way to apply permissions and access control collectively to a set of projects and users.

Roles GitLab SaaS offers various roles that define the level of access and permissions a user has within a project or group. The common roles include:

Owner The highest level of authority within a project or group. Owners have full control over the settings, members, and permissions.

Maintainer Maintainers have administrative privileges within a project or group. They can manage the project, including repositories, branches, and permissions.

Developer Developers have write access to the repository and can contribute code, create merge requests, and participate in project activities.

Reporter Reporters have read-only access and can view project information, including source code, issues, and merge requests. They cannot make any modifications.

Guest Guests have limited access and can only view basic project information without making any modifications.

Permissions Permissions define what actions a user can perform within a project or group. These actions may include creating and modifying repositories, pushing changes, managing issues and merge requests, modifying project settings, and more. GitLab SaaS allows administrators, maintainers, and owners to configure and customize permissions for each role within the system.

item.content:encoded:
Epic is an Electronic Medical Records (EMR) system used by hospitals and health systems. RSA G&L collects Epic data from Epic Clarity.

Clarity is Epic's relational reporting database (Oracle or Microsoft SQL Server). It holds an extract of the operational Epic database, so collection queries run without touching the production EMR.

Identities ❌ | Accounts ✔️ | Groups ❌ | App Roles ✔️ | Entitlements ❌
note

This guide covers Epic Clarity (SQL Server) as configured in the 2020–2023 timeframe. Column names may differ across Epic release versions.

Epic Objects​

Application​

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Application.
  3. Click on Create Application and select Other Application.
  4. Enter the details as shown below.
  5. Click Finish.

Account Collector​

This section explains the process for configuring an account collector for the Epic EMR application. We will use the SQL Server database collector for this purpose.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Applications.
  3. Click on Epic EMR.
  4. Navigate to Collectors tab and click on Create Account Collector. Enter the details as shown below.

  5. Click Next and enter the SQL Server database details. Use the Test Connection to make sure the connection details are accurate. Use the latest Microsoft JDBC Driver for SQL Server if NTLM authentication is required.

  6. Click Next. Select the appropriate data that you intend to collect. For the purpose of illustration we will collect accounts and user to account mapping from Epic EMR.

  7. Click Next. On the Account Data page, enter the following query to collect account information.
SELECT
  EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN EMP,
  EMP.PROV_ID AS SER,
  EMP.NAME AS displayName,
  EMP.USER_ID userID,
  CASE
    WHEN USER_STATUS_C = 1 THEN 0
    WHEN USER_STATUS_C = 2 THEN 1
    ELSE NULL
  END AS isDisabled,
  LAST_PW_UPDATE AS lastPasswordSetDate,
  LAST_ACCS_DATETIME AS lastLoginDate
FROM CLARITY_EMP EMP
WHERE EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN IS NOT NULL

The key column mappings for this step are:

RSA G&L FieldQuery AliasClarity ColumnNotes
EMPSYSTEM_LOGINUnique account identifier, used as the primary key
Display NamedisplayNameNAMEFull name of the provider or employee
External IDuserIDUSER_IDUsed in the user-to-account mapping query
Provider IDSERPROV_IDLinks to SER application entitlements
Account DisabledisDisabledUSER_STATUS_C1 (Active) → 0, 2 (Inactive) → 1, otherwise NULL
Last Password SetlastPasswordSetDateLAST_PW_UPDATE
Last LoginlastLoginDateLAST_ACCS_DATETIME


8. Click Next. On the User Account Mappings Data configuration page enter the following query to map the Epic EMR account to user identity.

SELECT
  EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN EMP,
  EMP.USER_ID userID
FROM CLARITY_EMP EMP
WHERE EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN IS NOT NULL
  1. Click Next. In the User Resolution Rules, map the user to account


  2. Click Finish. Use the Test function to make sure the configurations are accurate.

Entitlement Collector​

This section explains the process for configuring an entitlement collector to collect application roles (templates) from Epic EMR. We will use the SQL Server database collector for this purpose.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Applications.
  3. Click on Epic EMR.
  4. Navigate to Collectors tab and click on Create Entitlement Collector. Enter the details as shown below.

  5. Click Next and enter the database connection details as shown in Step 5 of Account Collector.
  6. Click Next. Select the data types that the collector will be collecting from Epic EMR.

  7. Click Next. On the General Column Names, map the attribute names.

  8. Click Next. Under Application Role Data section, use the following query to collect admin roles from Epic EMR.
SELECT DISTINCT
  TEMPLT_DSPLY_TITLE AS templateName,
  USER_ID AS template,
  TEMPLT_OWNER_PRIM_C AS owner
FROM CLARITY_EMP_2
WHERE TEMPLT_DSPLY_TITLE IS NOT NULL

The key column mappings for this step are:

RSA G&L FieldQuery AliasClarity ColumnNotes
templateNameTEMPLT_DSPLY_TITLETemplate display name shown in RSA G&L
templateUSER_IDInternal template identifier
OwnerownerTEMPLT_OWNER_PRIM_CPrimary owner category code


9. Click Next. On the Account Data section, enter the query below to collect mappings for account to roles.

SELECT
  TEMPLATE.LNK_TEMPLT_ID AS role_id,
  EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN AS account
FROM
  CLARITY_EMP EMP
  LEFT OUTER JOIN EMP_AVAIL_TEMPLT TEMPLATE ON TEMPLATE.USER_ID = EMP.USER_ID
WHERE
  TEMPLATE.LNK_TEMPLT_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN IS NOT NULL
UNION
SELECT
  SUBTEMPLATE.APPLD_SUBTMPLT_ID AS role_id,
  EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN AS account
FROM
  CLARITY_EMP EMP
  LEFT OUTER JOIN SUBTEMPLATES SUBTEMPLATE ON SUBTEMPLATE.USER_ID = EMP.USER_ID
WHERE
  SUBTEMPLATE.APPLD_SUBTMPLT_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND EMP.SYSTEM_LOGIN IS NOT NULL
caution

The SUBTEMPLATES table name varies across Epic deployments. Confirm the correct table name or view with your Epic DBA before running the collector.

  1. Click Next and then click Finish. Use the Test function to make sure the configurations are accurate.

Troubleshooting​

Test Connection Fails​

  • Root Cause: Incorrect database host or port, network firewall restrictions, missing JDBC driver, or unconfigured Windows authentication.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify the SQL Server hostname, port (default 1433), and Clarity database name are correct.
    2. Confirm the service account has network access to the Clarity database server.
    3. Ensure the Microsoft JDBC Driver for SQL Server is installed on the RSA G&L server.
    4. If using Windows or NTLM authentication, append integratedSecurity=true to the connection string.

SQL Query Returns Zero Rows​

  • Root Cause: Missing SYSTEM_LOGIN values in CLARITY_EMP or insufficient table permissions.
  • Resolution:
    1. Confirm SYSTEM_LOGIN is populated in CLARITY_EMP. Accounts without a system login are excluded by the WHERE clause.
    2. Verify the service account has SELECT permission on CLARITY_EMP, CLARITY_EMP_2, EMP_AVAIL_TEMPLT, and SUBTEMPLATES.

SUBTEMPLATES Table Not Found​

  • Root Cause: Schema variation across Epic deployment versions.
  • Resolution:
    1. Work with your Epic database administrator to verify the exact table or view name for subtemplates in your environment.
    2. Update the query mapping accordingly.

Collection Errors Mid-Run​

  • Root Cause: Database timeouts caused by clinical load spikes or network latency.
  • Resolution:
    1. Check the RSA G&L collection logs under Admin → Logs.
    2. Increase the JDBC connection timeout in the collector settings.
    3. Schedule the collector to run during off-peak clinical hours.

References​

Microsoft and Epic Documentation

  • Microsoft JDBC Driver for SQL Server: Connection string parameters, authentication configurations, and timeout settings.
  • Epic Systems Documentation and Developer Portal: Reporting specifications and Clarity relational data structures.
COL028

item.content:encoded:
RSA Authentication Manager is a robust solution for secure access control. It employs RSA's proprietary SecureID tokens, offering two-factor authentication. Users enter a unique token-generated code along with their password, enhancing security by requiring both something they know and something they have. The system ensures secure access to networks and applications.

Identities ❌ | Accounts ✔️ | Groups ✔️ | App Roles ❌ | Entitlements ✔️

Admin Roles in RSA Authentication Manager define permissions and responsibilities for system administrators, allowing them to manage user authentication and security settings.

Tokens in RSA Authentication Manager are physical or software-based devices that generate one-time passcodes. Users enter these passcodes during authentication, enhancing security.

Risk-Based Authentication in RSA Authentication Manager evaluates various factors such as user location, device, and behavior patterns to assess the risk level. Based on this assessment, it adapts the authentication process, adding or reducing security measures accordingly to mitigate potential risks.

Assumptions
  1. The PostgreSQL JDBC driver has been uploaded via the admin console.
  2. The RSA Authentication Manager certificate RSAAMTrustedRootSSLCA.crt has been imported via admin console.
  3. To enable RSA Identity G&L to connect to PostgreSQL database, a read only user has to be created using the rsautil manage-readonly-dbusers tool. Refer to SQL Access to the RSA Authentication Manager Database section in the RSA Authentication Manager 8.x Developer's Guide for detailed information.

Application​

The first step in collecting accounts, tokens information from RSA Authentication Manager is to create a placeholder application to store this information in RSA Identity G&L.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Application.
  3. Click on Create Application and select Other Application.
  4. Enter the details as shown below. If you intend to collect the account status and/or the locked status of the account configure the highlighted options.
  5. Click Finish.

Account Collector​

This section explains the process for configuring a account collector for the RSA Authentication Manager application. We will use the PostgreSQL database collector for this purpose.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Applications.
  3. Click on RSA Authentication Manager.
  4. Navigate to Collectors tab and click on Create Account Collector. Enter the details as shown below.

  5. Click Next and enter the PostgreSQL database connection details. Use the Test Connection to make sure the connection details are accurate.


  6. Click Next. Select the appropriate data that you intend to collect. For the purpose of illustration we will collect accounts, groups and user to account mapping from RSA Authentication Manager.

  7. Click Next. On the Account Data page, enter the following query to collect account information.
SELECT DISTINCT principalData.loginuid AS account
     ,login.login_date AS login_date
     ,CONCAT (principal.first_name, ' ', principal.last_name) AS full_name
     --1 = enabled, 2 = disabled 
     ,CASE
        WHEN principalData.lockout_flag = '1' THEN '1'
        ELSE '0'
      END AS account_locked
     ,securityDomain.NAME AS securityDomain_domain
     ,CASE
        WHEN principalData.security_ques_answers IS NULL THEN '0'
        ELSE '1'
      END AS securityDomain_questions,
       --1 = user is enabled, 0 = user is disabled
     CASE
        WHEN principalData.enable_flag = '1' THEN '0'
        ELSE '1'
      END AS account_status     
      --1 = user has administrative roles assigned
       --0 = user does not have any administrative roles assigned
     ,principalData.administrator_flag AS privileged
--Basic user settings
FROM IMS_PRINCIPAL principal
--Detailed information about the user
FULL JOIN IMS_PRINCIPAL_DATA principalData
     ON principal.loginuid = principalData.loginuid
--Information about the security domain
JOIN IMS_SECURITY_DOMAIN securityDomain
     ON principalData.owner_id = securityDomain.id
--Last logon date and time of the user      
JOIN IMS_PRINCIPAL_LOGIN_DATE login
     ON principalData.id = login.principal_id ‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍

The following are the important attributes


8. Click Next. On the User Account Mappings Data configuration page enter the following query to map the RSA Authentication Manager account to user identity.

SELECT DISTINCT
     loginuid,loginuid AS account
FROM 
     rsa_rep.IMS_PRINCIPAL_DATA

The following are the important attributes


9. Click Next. In the Group Data configuration section enter the following query to collect groups from RSA Authentication Manager.

SELECT DISTINCT
     (name) AS "group"
     ,description
FROM
     rsa_rep.IMS_GROUP_DATA
-- Optional Filter 
WHERE  
     identity_src_id = 'The Identity Source ID'

The following are the important attributes


10. In the Account Membership Data configuration section enter the following query to collect groups membership information from RSA Authentication Manager.

SELECT 
     accounts.loginuid AS account
    ,GROUPS.name AS "group"
FROM rsa_rep.IMS_PRINCIPAL_DATA accounts
JOIN rsa_rep.IMS_PRINCIPAL_GROUP groupMembership
     ON accounts.id = groupMembership.principal_id
JOIN rsa_rep.IMS_GROUP_DATA GROUPS
     ON groupMembership.group_id = GROUPS.id
-- Optional Filter
WHERE
     GROUPS.identity_src_id = 'The Identity Source Identitfier'

Entitlement Collector : Admin Roles​

This section explains the process for configuring a entitlement collector to collect admin roles from RSA Authentication Manager application. We will use the PostgreSQL database collector for this purpose.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as AveksaAdmin.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Applications.

  8. Click Next. Under Application Role Data section, use the following query to collect admin roles from RSA Authentication Manager.
SELECT 
     name AS AppRole
     ,description
FROM
     IMS_ADMIN_ROLE

The following are the important attributes

SELECT 
     users.loginuid AS Account
     ,ROLES.name AS AppRole
FROM IMS_PRINCIPAL_DATA users
JOIN IMS_PRINCIPAL_ADMIN_ROLE admins
     ON users.id = admins.principal_id
JOIN IMS_ADMIN_ROLE ROLES
     ON admins.admin_role_id = ROLES.id

Entitlement Collector : Tokens​

This section explains the process for configuring a entitlement collector to collect tokens as account entitlements from RSA Authentication Manager application. We will use the PostgreSQL database collector for this purpose.

Steps

  1. Login to RSA G&L console as AveksaAdmin.
  2. Navigate to Resources > Applications.
  3. Click on RSA Authentication Manager.
  4. Navigate to Collectors tab and click on Create Entitlement Collector. Enter the details as shown below.

  5. Click Next and enter the database connection details as shown in Step 5 of Account Collector.
  6. Click Next. Select the data types that the collector will be collecting from RSA Authentication Manager.

  7. Click Next. On the General Column Names, map the attribute names.

  8. Click Next.
  9. Click Next on the Resource Data page.
  10. Click Next. Under Resource Entitlement Data section, use the following query to collect tokens information from RSA Authentication Manager.
SELECT 
     tokens.serial_number AS RESOURCE
     ,CASE
        WHEN tokens.token_type = '0' THEN 'Std Card'
        WHEN tokens.token_type = '1' THEN 'PIN Pad'
        WHEN tokens.token_type = '2' THEN 'SID 700'
        WHEN tokens.token_type = '4' THEN 'Soft Token'
        WHEN tokens.token_type = '9' THEN 'SID 800'
        WHEN tokens.token_type = '10' THEN 'Flex Card'
      END               AS Action
     ,tokens.token_shutdown_date AS Expiration
     ,tokenDetails.last_login_date     AS lastlogin,
     CASE
        WHEN tokens.is_enabled = 'true' OR tokens.is_enabled = 't' THEN 'true'
        ELSE 'false'
     END as tokenEnabled
FROM   AM_TOKEN tokens
     ,AM_TOKEN_OOB tokenDetails
WHERE  tokens.id = tokenDetails.am_token_id‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍
  1. Click Next. On the Account Data section, enter the query below to collect mappings for account to tokens.
SELECT users.loginuid   AS Account
     ,serial_number AS RESOURCE
     ,CASE
        WHEN token_type = '0' THEN 'Std Card'
        WHEN token_type = '1' THEN 'PIN Pad'
        WHEN token_type = '2' THEN 'SID 700'
        WHEN token_type = '4' THEN device.family_key
        WHEN token_type = '9' THEN 'SID 800'
        WHEN token_type = '10' THEN 'Flex Card'
      END         AS Action
FROM IMS_PRINCIPAL_DATA users

Entitlement Collector : Risk Based Authentication​

This section explains the process for configuring a entitlement collector to collect information regarding Risk Based Authentication (RBA) being enabled for an account from RSA Authentication Manager application. We will use the PostgreSQL database collector for this purpose.

Steps
